# INKWELL

> Photograph something you wrote. Get back a transparent, print-ready mark that
> still looks like ink.

INKWELL extracts hand-inked marks from photographs into an alpha channel. It never
thresholds the image. The greyscale ramp of the photograph becomes the alpha
channel directly, so the anti-aliased stroke edge, the pressure variation and the
dry-marker skip all survive. A hard cut discards them and leaves a flat silhouette
that reads as clip art.

Two corrections land before that ramp is usable, and both come from the camera
rather than the ink. Paper is not white: a phone meters for the dark marks, so
printer paper returns around luma 185. Lighting is not even: there is a gradient
across the sheet. Flat-field correction solves both by dilating the image past the
stroke width, which erases the ink and leaves a map of how the sheet was lit, then
dividing the original by that map.

Grain and edge artifacts are removed by finding the cliff in the component size
distribution rather than applying a fixed threshold. Ink runs orders of magnitude
larger than grain, and the gap sits somewhere different in every photograph.

## Privacy

Everything runs on the device. No upload, no server, no account, no network call
of any kind. The fonts are served from this origin for the same reason. A
signature is a credential.

## Surfaces

- Live tool: https://inkwell.puddystudios.com/
- Source: https://github.com/cubedivisiondev/inkwell
- Command line and library: pip install inkwell-ink
